lines.trans: Max, we urgently need to clarify something.
Guys, I really do not have time for you now.
What did you tell Nastya about me?
I was just joking a little, do not be mad.
Joking? You called me a real psycho!
I wanted to protect you from mistakes.
First you promised to help, and then bailed!
I did not want to hurt you, Kostya.
Because of your stupid words Nastya left.
Forgive me, I will fix everything today.
Never poke your nose into my business again!
Kostya, wait, let us discuss everything calmly.
Some best friend you are, leave!

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?
We need to do even more.
I don't need any more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid?
That was a silly joke.

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up

examples.trans: Let's clean up!
See you, bye!
Arkasha, let's clean up!

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.
Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
He's my friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

злиться.gloss: to be angry, to get mad

meanings.en: to be angry, to get mad

examples.text: А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: And do you know why you are so angry?
Don't be angry with me, please.

examples.text: Хорошо. А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: Fine. Do you know why you're so angry?

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.en: to fix, to correct, to put right
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, to correct', paired with 'исправлять'.

examples.trans: Excuse us, we will fix everything.

examples.text: Ученик быстро исправил ошибку в тетради.
examples.trans: The pupil quickly corrected the mistake in his notebook.

examples.text: Да, вы знаете, это очень серьёзная операция. Мы всё исправим. До свидания!
examples.trans: Yes, you know, it is a very serious operation. We'll fix everything. Goodbye!

кинуть.gloss: to throw, to toss, to fling

meanings.en: to throw, to toss, to hurl

examples.trans: We'll throw a bottle through her window.
The boy threw the ball to the dog.

examples.text: Мы её сильно напугаем! Бутылку кинем ей в окно.
examples.trans: We will scare her badly! We'll throw a bottle through her window.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'something, a thing or two' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And one more thing.
I want to show you something.

examples.text: И ещё кое-что. Эдуард Владимирович просил передать привет.
examples.trans: And one more thing. Eduard Vladimirovich asked us to pass on his regards.

лезть.gloss: to climb; to push in, to barge in

meanings.note: лезть на дерево = to climb a tree

meanings.en: to push in, to barge in
meanings.note: лезть без очереди = to jump the queue; лезть вперёд кого-то = to push in ahead of someone
colloquial: не лезь! = keep out of it!

examples.trans: Don't jump the queue!
The cat is climbing the tree.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world

examples.trans: This is the best day!
You're my best friend.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.
You called me a real psycho!

examples.text: Пошутил? Ты назвал меня настоящим маньяком!
examples.trans: Joking? You called me a real psycho!
Where's my toy car?
That's mine.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

наговорить.gloss: to say a lot of (too much)

meanings.en: to say a lot of, blurt out too much
meanings.note: + genitive: наговорить лишнего = to say too much

examples.trans: Yesterday I said too much to you.
He said a lot of foolish things.

examples.text: Что ты про меня наговорил Насте?
examples.trans: What did you tell Nastya about me?

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: of things, places, films: 'как называется ...?' = what is ... called?

examples.trans: What's this town called?
The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.trans: Never!

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.
You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
He didn't want to offend anyone.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. And what are you doing here?

examples.text: Без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: Without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.
The partners discussed the terms of the deal in detail.

examples.text: Заодно без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: At the same time without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.
A letter from Mum.
I'm tired of work.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
This is some kind of mistake!
Sorry, I made a mistake.
There are many serious mistakes in the case.
Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Maybe you could help?
Of course I'll help.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'обещать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to promise', paired with 'обещать'.

examples.text: Он сегодня пообещал построить нам новое здание.
examples.trans: Today he promised to build us a new building.
She promised to help.

examples.text: А вот Павел Юрьевич нам помог! Он сегодня пообещал построить нам новое здание.
examples.trans: Whereas Pavel Yuryevich helped us! Today he promised to build us a new building.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: First coffee, then work.
I'll call later.
And then waste will flow.

пошутить.gloss: to joke, to make a joke

meanings.note: я пошутил(а) = I was only joking

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!
Don't be offended, I was only joking.

examples.text: Может быть, шеф просто неудачно пошутил?
examples.trans: Maybe the chef was just joking unsuccessfully?

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.
She knows everything about everyone.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.
Excuse me, who are you?
Forgive me.
Please forgive me.
I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!
We urgently need to clarify something.

examples.text: Макс, нам нужно срочно кое-что прояснить.
examples.trans: Max, we urgently need to clarify something.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!

examples.trans: Guys, where are you?
The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.
I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.
I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.trans: But you gave your word!
He keeps his word.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.
He's completely alone.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You'll do everything calmly.
He sat calmly.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!
I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.
This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Я хотел уберечь тебя от ошибок.
examples.trans: I wanted to protect you from mistakes.

examples.text: Мой долг уберечь вас от этого.
examples.trans: It's my duty to protect you from this.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: I want him to leave.
She has already gone home.
So should I leave?

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)

examples.trans: Go away!
I'm going home.
You are. Go away.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.
What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
